column2: Knead a dough with the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, water and oil and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Knead the mince with the finely chopped vegetables and spices (without cooking).
Divide the dough into 4 and roll each into a boat shape.
Spread the filling and fold up the edges.
Bake at 250 °C for 12–15 minutes.
Preheat the oven at its highest setting.
Hot, with ayran.
Lahmacun (homemade)
1 long green pepper
1 dessert spoon chilli flakes, salt
Knead the dough and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Blitz the onion, tomato, pepper and parsley in a food processor and knead with the mince, tomato paste and spices.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll out very thinly.
Spread the filling in a thin layer.
Bake on a preheated tray at 250 °C for 8–10 minutes.
The filling must be spread thinly; if thick, it won’t cook.
With lemon and greens.
Cooked lahmacun can be frozen.
Potato gözleme (griddle style)
3 boiled potatoes
Knead a soft dough with the flour, water and salt and rest for 20 minutes.
Mash the potatoes and mix with fried onion and chilli flakes.
Divide the dough into 4 and roll out thinly.
Spread the filling over half and fold over.
Cook in a dry pan for 3 minutes on each side and brush with butter.
The dough should be thin.
Simit (sesame bread rings)
1 dessert spoon salt and sugar
1.5 cups lukewarm water
Half a cup grape molasses
1 cup water (for the molasses)
1.5 cups sesame
Divide into 8, split each piece in two, roll into long thin ropes, twist together and form into rings.
Dip in the molasses water and coat in toasted sesame.
Rest on the tray for 15 minutes.
Bake at 220 °C for 18–20 minutes.
Toasting the sesame first boosts the aroma.
With tea and cheese.
Same day; can be frozen.
Cheese pişi (fried dough)
Divide into balls and flatten by hand.
Put cheese in the centre, close and flatten slightly.
Fry in hot oil until browned on each side.
The oil shouldn’t be too hot, or the outside burns before the inside cooks.
Hot, for breakfast.
Yeasted açma (with olives)
Half a cup chopped olives
Knead a soft dough with the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk, oil and egg white and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Divide into 12 and roll out thinly.
Sprinkle with olives, roll up and join into a ring.
Brush with egg yolk and rest for 20 minutes.
Bake at 180 °C for 25 minutes.
The second rise is the key to softness.
2 days in a closed container.
Kol böreği (potato roll börek)
4 boiled potatoes
Mash the potatoes and mix with fried onion and spices.
Mix the milk and oil.
Cut the yufka sheets in half, moisten with the sauce, put filling along the edge and roll up.
Arrange in a spiral in a round tray and brush with egg yolk.
Bake at 190 °C for 35 minutes.
The potato filling must be cold.
Bazlama (flatbread)
Knead all the ingredients into a soft dough and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Divide into 6 balls and rest for 15 minutes.
Flatten by hand to 1 cm thick.
Cook in a dry, hot pan for 3–4 minutes on each side; turn once it puffs up.
Cover with a cloth to cool.
Covering with a cloth keeps the bazlama soft.
Hot, for breakfast.
Hünkar beğendi (beef on smoky eggplant purée)
600 g diced beef
Beğendi: 4 eggplants, 2 tablespoons butter, 2 tablespoons flour, 1.5 cups milk, half a cup grated kashar
Fry the meat in butter until its liquid evaporates, then add the onion and tomato paste.
Cook with the tomato and 2 glasses of hot water over low heat for 75 minutes until the meat is tender.
Char the eggplants, peel and chop finely.
Toast the flour in butter, add the milk and thicken; stir in the eggplant and kashar.
Spread the beğendi on a plate and put the meat in the middle.
If you keep the eggplant in lemon water, it won’t darken.
3 days in a closed container in the fridge; 3 months in the freezer.
Orman kebabı (forest stew)
10 pearl onions
Fry the meat in butter.
Add the pearl onions and tomato paste.
Cook with 2 glasses of hot water for 45 minutes.
Add the diced carrot, potato and peas and cook for 25 more minutes.
Serve with thyme.
Don’t add the vegetables before the meat is tender.
Slow-roasted lamb (tandır, in the oven)
1.5 kg lamb shoulder or leg
6 garlic cloves
1 dessert spoon thyme and rosemary
Make cuts in the meat with a knife and insert the garlic.
Rub with oil and spices.
Put in a roasting dish with water and cover tightly with foil.
Roast at 160 °C for 2.5–3 hours, until the meat comes away from the bone.
Remove the foil and brown at 220 °C for 15 minutes.
Low heat over a long time is the secret to tenderness.
With rice pilaf and roasted vegetables.
İzmir köfte
500 g minced meat
1 onion (grated)
1 dessert spoon salt, cumin, black pepper
Knead the mince, onion, egg, breadcrumbs and spices and shape into finger köfte.
Pre-bake the köfte and potato wedges at 200 °C for 15 minutes.
Arrange the köfte, potatoes, peppers and tomatoes in turn on the tray.
Dissolve the tomato paste in 1.5 glasses of hot water and pour over.
Bake at 180 °C for 30 minutes.
Pre-baking keeps the köfte from falling apart.
Tas kebabı (bowl stew)
600 g diced beef
Cook the meat until it reabsorbs its own juices.
Add the butter and onion and fry for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and tomatoes.
Cook with hot water over low heat for 70 minutes.
In a pressure cooker, 30 minutes is enough.
Eggplant moussaka with minced meat
Peel the eggplants in stripes and slice into rounds; soak in salted water for 15 minutes and pat dry.
Brush the eggplants with oil and roast at 200 °C for 15 minutes.
Fry the mince with the onion, pepper and tomato paste.
